subject: Clarify billing impact of SentencePiece vs BPE across hosted models
messages:
From: Megan Brooks <megan.brooks@nimbushealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@nimbushealth.com
Date: Thu, 05 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Rate card + tokenization question for hosted API

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Nimbus is very interested in Redwood for clinical note summarization. Procurement asked that we get a clear written answer on billing behavior before we proceed: how do token counts differ across models that use SentencePiece (e.g., some of the newer open models) vs BPE-based models (GPT-style), and how should we expect that to affect per-token pricing and the estimate you provided on our expected monthly spend?

Specifically:
- Are tokens billed based on the model's tokenizer (i.e., actual encoder tokens) or do you normalize token counts across models in the hosted API?
- For longer clinical notes (~2k words average), do SentencePiece-first models produce materially different token counts that would change our cost by +/-% ranges?

If you can include any sample tokenization deltas or a short appendix we can share with procurement, that would help. Also attaching our monthly volume snapshot (NIMBUS_MLP_Octets-usage.csv) for reference.

Best,
Megan
Procurement | Nimbus Health
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Megan Brooks <megan.brooks@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Rate card + tokenization question for hosted API

Hi Megan — great question and thanks for the usage file. High level answer first, then details below so procurement can paste into the SOW: 

Short answer: billing on Redwood hosted API is based on the model-specific tokenizer (we bill per-token as produced by the model's encoder). That means token counts can vary between SentencePiece and BPE tokenizers; in practice for long clinical text we typically see a 5–18% range depending on language, punctuation density, and the specific model family.

Attached: Redwood_Ratecard_v2.xlsx and a brief tokenization appendix with sample deltas (tokenization-billing-appendix.pdf). Key points you can give procurement:
- Billing = encoder tokens produced by the model variant you call. We do not normalize behind the scenes for hosted endpoints.
- For customer-facing budgeting we provide a "model equivalence" table (see appendix) that maps common models to a normalized tokens-per-1k-words estimate so you can forecast cost across options.
- If you pick a model family for production, we can run a quick batch on your sample notes and produce an exact projected monthly token count for your observed distribution.

Operational options to control cost:
- Use a BPE-based variant for lower token density when output style tolerates it.
- Apply our prefix/KV caching for repeated clinical headers (saves up to 30% on recurring tokens).
- Use Redwood Optimize recommendations (we can run an evaluation to see if 8-bit quantized variants preserve quality for your prompts).

Marcus / Stephanie — I think Nimbus will want a committed discount schedule if they commit to a 12-month reserved tier. Marcus, can you pull the suggested discount bands for ~200M tokens/mo baseline?

Megan — short next step: if you share a 2–3 day sample of raw notes we’ll run a tokenization parity job and return per-model estimates.

— Priya
Director, Solutions | Redwood Inference
(priya.natarajan@redwood.ai)

Attachment stubs: Redwood_Ratecard_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), tokenization-billing-appendix.pdf (pdf)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 06 Feb 2026 08:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Rate card + tokenization question for hosted API

Thanks Priya — quick pricing note from my side:

For a 12-month commitment at ~200M tokens/month we typically offer the following tiers (these are starting points; final bands depend on exact commit and any add-ons):
- 200M/mo: 10% off list hosted per-token rates
- 500M/mo: 16% off
- 1B+/mo: custom pricing and SOW, includes single-tenant routing and higher support SLA

We treat the per-token list price as model-agnostic in the ratecard, but since token counts differ by model we show an "effective cost per 1M words" projection in the appendix to make comparisons apples-to-apples. For Nimbus specifically, if SentencePiece models push you +12% tokens on average vs the BPE baseline, then the effective spend at month-end will reflect that delta — the discount applies to billed tokens.

Two negotiable levers for procurement:
1) A small markup to lock in a model-equivalence cap (we can cap effective billing so if your token delta vs baseline exceeds X% we credit back the overage for first 3 months while we tune prompts).
2) Commit-and-refund: if you commit to 12 months and usage under-runs the commit in month 1–3 we apply credits to future invoices.

Happy to draft language for the SOW. Priya — we should propose the cap option as a procurement-friendly concession.

— Marcus
Head of Sales | Redwood Inference

If those look good we’ll move to a formal quote. I can loop in legal after we have SOW text.

Megan — all good. Next steps:

1) Tokenization parity job: we can accept sanitized sample upload to a secure S3 bucket. I sent upload instructions and the access form to procurement (see Drive link). Once we have the sample we'll run a parity job and return a per-model token report within 48 business hours.

2) Draft SOW language: attached is a short draft clause in the tokenization appendix (also pasted below) that describes the model-equivalence cap mechanics. Key points:
- Measurement window: monthly billed tokens across the agreed production endpoint(s).
- Baseline comparator: BPE baseline model agreed in SOW (e.g., redwood-bpe-lite-v1).
- Cap trigger: if average monthly token delta > 8% vs baseline over first 3 billing cycles, Redwood will issue a credit equal to the billed excess tokens above the 8% threshold, up to a cap equal to 3 months of committed usage.
- Reporting: Redwood delivers a monthly token report and parity appendices as part of the billing packet.

Marcus — please include the proposed discount bands in the quote and mark the cap as an optional add-on.

Megan — I'll open the HubSpot deal and attach the DocuSign quote link once legal gives the final SOW text.
